In this section, we present InfiniGen, a KV cache management framework for
offloading-based inference systems. We first show the high-level overview of
our proposed KV cache management solution (Section 4.1) and
discuss the opportunities of KV cache prefetching that we
observe (Section 4.2).
We then explain our prefetching module (Section 4.3), which builds on
the offloading-based inference systems, and discuss how InfiniGen manages the KV [...] In this work, we propose InfiniGen, a KV cache management framework designed to
synergistically work with modern offloading-based inference systems.
InfiniGen builds on two key design principles.
First, it speculates and chooses the KV cache entries that are critical to
produce the next output token, dropping the non-critical ones, by conducting a
minimal rehearsal of attention computation for Layer ii at Layer i−1i-1. [...] ## 6 Analysis and Discussion

### 6.1 Sensitivity Study

We use the OPT-6.7B model with 1920 input tokens, 128 output tokens, and a
batch size of 8. The accuracy is evaluated with the WinoGrande task in
lm-evaluation-harness.

results.title: Medium
results.content:
Generating long content with LLMs presents a challenge due to the substantial memory requirements of the transient state, known as the key-value (KV) cache, which scales with sequence length and batch size. This blog reviews InfiniGen, a novel KV cache management framework designed specifically for long-text generation, which integrates seamlessly with modern offloading-based inference systems, which leverage larger CPU memory. InfiniGen leverages a key insight: only a few essential tokens are [...] tokens are necessary to compute the attention layers of Transformers in subsequent steps. By speculating on these critical tokens using the inputs of the current layer and part of the query weight and key cache of the next layer, InfiniGen enables prefetching of only the essential KV cache entries, thus reducing fetch overhead from host CPU memory in offloading-based LLM systems.
